The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) is an Ethiopian political and former armed organization whose decades of political dominance have been accompanied by extensive criticism over authoritarian governance, suppression of political opposition, restrictions on civil liberties, and serious human-rights abuses. The TPLF emerged as a Marxist-Leninist guerrilla movement and became the dominant force within the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF), the coalition that ruled Ethiopia after overthrowing the Derg regime in 1991.

During the EPRDF period, Human Rights Watch reported that the TPLF-led government used political repression to consolidate its control, including harassment and arbitrary detention of opposition supporters, restrictions on independent organizations and media, and pressure against political dissent. In Oromia, Human Rights Watch documented arrests, torture, harassment and restrictions against people suspected of supporting opposition movements, while describing the political environment as one in which genuine political competition was severely restricted.

The TPLF's political dominance was particularly controversial because its influence extended far beyond its regional base in Tigray. Through the EPRDF coalition and affiliated regional parties, it exercised substantial influence over Ethiopia's national political and security institutions. Human Rights Watch reported that the ruling coalition consolidated political control through intimidation, restrictions on opposition activity, and the use of state resources and institutions to weaken political challengers.

The TPLF again became a central actor in Ethiopian politics during the Tigray War, which began in November 2020 after the political confrontation between the Tigray regional government and Ethiopia's federal government escalated into armed conflict. During the war, forces affiliated with the TPLF were accused of serious violations against civilians, including unlawful killings, looting, destruction of property and sexual violence. These allegations form part of a wider record of grave abuses committed by multiple parties to the conflict.

The organization's legacy is therefore deeply contested. Supporters credit the TPLF with helping overthrow the Derg dictatorship, introducing ethnic federalism and playing a major role in Ethiopia's political transformation after 1991. Critics, however, point to its prolonged political dominance, suppression of opposition and the serious abuses documented during periods of conflict and political repression. Human Rights Watch's reporting provides extensive documentation of the restrictions and abuses associated with the TPLF-led government, while also emphasizing that serious violations have been committed by multiple Ethiopian actors rather than by the TPLF alone.

rule:
Every change to an article's short description ({{Short description|...}}: the line Wikipedia
shows under the title in its search box and apps), up to the analysed revision.

Method, by fixed rules:
- The page history from 1 January 2017 (cached revision IDs) is checked at up to 128 evenly
  spaced revisions, always including the first of that period and the analysed one; a short
  description already there at the first is reported as present on that date. Only the opening section's wikitext is read
  (the template sits there), 50 revisions per request.
- Also checked: every edit whose summary mentions the short description, and every edit
  Wikipedia tagged as later reverted (summaries are read only to choose these and are not kept).
- Wherever two neighbouring checkpoints differ, the revisions between them are checked the same
  way, narrowing down until the exact edit is found: the revision whose short description differs
  from its predecessor's.
- Limits: a change undone before the next checkpoint (for example vandalism and its repair) can
  be missed when both checkpoints show the same text; the gap between checkpoints is stated with
  the result. A revision whose text Wikipedia has hidden is skipped; when a change falls inside a run
  of hidden revisions, it is dated to the first visible revision after them. A maintenance tag inside the
  description (such as {{Disputed inline}}) is shown by name. Until about 2018 most short
  descriptions came from Wikidata rather than the article; those are not in the article's
  history and are not tracked here.
`wtl shortdesc` writes data/shortdesc.json. No usernames are stored.
